title: Reading the street before you step into it
target: What is actually happening outside the shop in Supermarket Simulator, so going out to the street is a decision rather than a gamble.
version: 1.6.0 (223), read from the copy of the game this site was built from (see the sources page)
prerequisites: A shop with a street outside it
Some reason to go out — a delivery, a pump or a vehicle

steps.do: Treat the street as a place of its own rather than as scenery.
steps.because: the roads are objects of their own — a base, a creator, a drawer and a loader — and a road knows its connections (RoadBase, RoadCreator, RoadDrawer, RoadsLoader, RoadConnectionsBase)

steps.do: Watch the traffic rather than the markings.
steps.because: traffic follows waypoints that carry data of their own, with a navigator working along them (WaypointData, WaypointNavigator)

steps.do: Cross where a light is reporting a state rather than where it looks clear.
steps.because: a traffic light reports a change of its own state (TrafficLight, TrafficLightChanged)

steps.do: Expect a vehicle to change lanes as part of its route, not as a warning to you.
steps.because: changing lanes is part of following a route (LaneChange)

steps.do: Remember who is holding the traffic together.
steps.because: the street's traffic is run by a manager and a holder of its own (NPCTrafficManager, TrafficHolder)

steps.do: In a shared shop, expect the traffic to be shared too.
steps.because: the street's traffic has a shared form as well as a local one (TrafficComponent, TrafficComponentMultiplayer)

steps.do: Know what is actually out there before you plan a trip.
steps.because: the street has a petrol station with a pump, street lighting with a controller behind it, and deliveries and storage tied to the street (GasStationPump, StreetLights, StreetLightController, StreetBoxTarget, StorageStreet)

commonMistakes: Stepping out because the road looks empty rather than because a light says so.
Assuming a vehicle that is changing lanes has seen you.
Forgetting that a delivery can be tied to the street rather than to the shop floor.
Treating the road as something drawn rather than something built from its own pieces.
sources: A local copy of the game, read only. Grounding for each step is on the technical reference pages; no number is estimated.
